title: Poisson kernel-defect limit for sparse uniform planar or unicellular rooted maps at a finite cubic sparsity crossover
source_title: The mesoscopic geometry of sparse random maps
author: Nicolas Curien; Igor Kortchemski; Cyril Marzouk
difficulty_reason: A pointwise enumeration ratio is insufficient to determine the defect law because mass could escape through arbitrarily large defects. Sections2–3 prove the exact core-kernel enumeration and uniform near-trivalent contraction ratios, transferring loop controls through Catalan-weighted forests. Section4 combines those new estimates with a uniform factorial tail to normalize the finite-crossover Poisson law, so its difficulty is not the final ratio-to-Poisson calculation alone.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Theorem1(1) only: uniform rooted maps with n edges, either planar with s_n faces or unicellular of genus(s_n-1)/2 (odd s_n), s_n tending to infinity and s_n/n tending to zero, n^(-1/3)s_n tending to finite a>=0. Exact Poisson mean3(1-lambda_circ)sqrt(3 a³/2), lambda_circ=1-sqrt(3)/2 planar and0 unicellular. PDF physical6 rendered to verify formula despite replacement glyphs in text extraction. Complete exact decomposition11–13, uniform saddle-point Lemma8 full14–16, Catalan contractions/defect ratios18–25 and finite-regime ratio/factorial-tail proof25–26 read. Existing cycle lemma, Budzinski planar loop large deviations, Walsh–Lehman enumeration, Wormald switching and classical UIPT loop density are explicit published research foundations. Lemma8 bounded crude-product comparisons omit only algebra with the immediately supplied product13 and explicit endpoint inequalities; no new asymptotic construction supplied. Unicellular ratio proof uses the same fully written planar argument with its separately supplied non-loop concentration25. Theorem1(2) has negative deviation proof explicitly left to reader on26 and is excluded, as are core-size/mesoscopic geometry and enumeration corollaries. One combined two-model primary theorem part, no additional parameter cases counted.
